messages:
tamara: Heads-up — I opened PR #1423 to split the gpu_pool module into gpu_pool_core + gpu_pool_v2 and migrate VPC/IAM/KMS inputs. This is a structural change not a behavioral change, but it renames a few inputs (kms_alias -> kms_key_id, vpc_map -> subnet_map) and adds a 'stable' vs 'edge' channel for provider pinning. Rollout plan below.

ryan: Nice. timeline? are we changing any TF state shapes that require import/move? :eyes:

tamara: Short timeline: canary deploy next Tue (us-west-2), then europe-west1 the following Tue. No state file rewrites — we keep existing resource addresses. There's a transitional shim that maps old var names to new ones for one release. We'll remove shim in v3.

sasha: Can you paste the shim snippet? want to audit before canary.

tamara: Sure — example in the PR.

```
# modules/gpu_pool_v2/variables.tf
variable "kms_key_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "KMS key ID (new name, accepts old alias via shim)"
}

# root module (shim)
locals {
  kms_key_id = coalesce(var.kms_key_id, var.kms_alias)
  subnet_map = coalesce(var.subnet_map, var.vpc_map)
}
```

kevin: Question: during canary, if autoscaler spins up new nodes will quotas in eu-west1 blow our budget? we had spot fallback issues last quarter.

tamara: Good call. Canary policy includes quota guard: terraform plan CI will run a quota-check script and fail if requested GPUs + current usage > soft_limit. Deploy-bot will also gate canary merges until quota check passes.

infra-bot: CI:terraform-plan for PR #1423 finished — 0 diffs against canary-org workspace (no surprise changes). Logs: https://ci.redwood/infra/1423/plan

ryan: For the rollback story — what if the shim ends up causing unexpected IAM bindings? how do we revert quickly?

tamara: Rollback steps (short):
1) pin module source in root module to previous tag (git ref v2.18.1)
2) run `terraform plan -var-file=canary.tfvars` and verify no drifts
3) apply to canary, then to prod once verified.

sasha: Recommend adding an automated post-merge job to detect IAM diffs and alert SRE. I can add a check to the gitops CI that diffs iam_policy JSONs and fails if anything non-empty.

kevin: Also add a node-drain pre-stop hook for rolling deletes, last time a manual drain was missed and we got 15 pods stuck. :grimacing:

tamara: Agreed — I'll attach a helm hook that ensures `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` runs as part of the rollout job for GPU nodegroups.

ryan: cc @sasha @kevin please review PR comments about provider aliasing. We changed provider alias propagation to use a stable channel variable to avoid provider lockfile churn.

sasha: On provider lockfile churn — my plan: add a lockfile manifest per-region that the release manager can bump manually. CI will refuse merges that modify the lockfile without an approved release note. That should prevent accidental auto-bumps.

infra-bot: Canary deploy scheduled for 2026-03-24 02:00 UTC (us-west-2). Reminder will post 1h before.

tamara: Docs added in the PR: migration.md covers variable mapping, rollback commands, and the provider-lock policy. Please leave reviews. :thumbsup:

ryan: LGTM except for one question in the PR thread re: kms key permissions. I'll drop a review comment.

kevin: If we see quota pressure during canary, we should have an immediate fallback to the old gpupool module in the gitops channel. Is that a manual flip or do we automate?

tamara: Plan is manual for safety but we've scripted the flip: update module source ref -> run quick-apply job that only affects module block. Script: `scripts/revert_module.sh v2.18.1 canary` — can be run by oncall. I'll add runbook to the PR.

sasha: Sounds good. I'll add the IAM diff check and the lockfile gating tomorrow AM.

deploy-bot: noted — canary window reserved. If any manual revert is required, notify #eng-oncall and tag `@oncall`.
